title: Vegetable Guides — natural growing scenes, second set

user_feedback.reason: Natural subject matter, rather than composition. Crops growing in place and candid gardening activity preferred.
user_feedback.disliked_subjects: Arranged harvests (3 and 4) and posed standing portrait (5).
user_feedback.clarification: John explicitly confirmed that '6 is posed' meant 5.

scope: Another set of six photographic concepts for Vegetable Guides, current folio 7. Selected images will be redrawn full-size later.

request.prompt:
Use case: photorealistic-natural.
Create ONE NEW photographic contact sheet containing SIX different candidate photographs for the Vegetable Guides section opener of The Vegetable Guru, a British gardening book. User feedback on the first round: likes living growing beds, real allotment views and candid activity; dislikes arranged harvest still lifes and posed portraits. The NEW set must embody an ordinary productive real garden, observed during use. No harvest displays, baskets, vegetables on a table or smiling at camera.

CONTACT SHEET GEOMETRY IS IMPORTANT: one NEAR-SQUARE LANDSCAPE overall canvas approximately 1660 pixels WIDE by 1500 pixels HIGH, THREE columns by TWO rows. Each photograph is a moderately tall PORTRAIT rectangle at 185:240, about 520px wide × 675px high. Do NOT make narrow phone-shaped photos. Equal-size panels. Narrow warm-white gutters. Separate narrow label strips BELOW the photos, numerals 1,2,3 in top row and 4,5,6 in bottom row. Only these numbers; no titles or other text anywhere.

Actual input references:
Image 1 H31 — real HOME GARDEN camera view from beside greenhouse glazing back towards vegetable planting, hedge and low pale wall. The slab path runs beside the glass on the right, herb trough beside the bed, courgette and bean foliage. Use its real small garden scale, materials, bed edges, irregular path and relationships in panels 1, 2 and 5. Reframe/crop the supported view rather than inventing architecture.
Image 2 A31 — real ALLOTMENT camera view across planted strips and bean supports towards John's small pale green shed, adjacent black water butt and paving. The brown shed belongs to a neighbour. Use this actual setting for panels 4 and 6.
Image 3 A43 — real AUGUST ALLOTMENT view at leek height, pale netted bed beyond, slab path at right and cropped green shed/black butt at upper right. Use directly for panel 3. Preserve actual uneven sizes and density, soil gaps, leaning foliage.
Image 4 LOOKDOWN — John's mandatory real downward-profile reference sheet. Use the actual camera photos, not the illustrated tile, to preserve his face when looking down in panels 5 and 6. No cap or winter clothing in these new summer scenes. His short grey beard slopes back towards throat, lower lip ahead of chin, no exaggerated projecting beard or chin.
Image 5 J02 — real John in July home garden: his identity, mature body proportions, hair and summer clothes, and second-angle garden context. Same olive T-shirt and olive shorts in panels 5 and 6, bareheaded, short receding greying hair and short grey beard. Omit microphone. His pose here is NOT to be copied: the new figures are absorbed in gardening, unposed and never making eye contact.

PHOTOGRAPHIC CHARACTER: realistic editorial photography of a small productive Cornish garden/allotment. Soft bright summer daylight, natural greens with restrained colour accents, true leaf and soil detail. Plants of differing sizes and ages, some overlapping, some bare soil, a few picked-leaf scars, occasional small insect nibbles. Modest traces of grass along path edges. Healthy and cared for but clearly worked and lived in. No garden-show perfection, no artificial abundance, no repeating leaf arrangements, no huge vegetables, no theatrical golden lighting, no HDR, no plastic shine, no CGI.

SIX NEW PHOTOGRAPHS:
1. A WALK THROUGH THE HOME VEGETABLE GARDEN — no person. Portrait camera view from beside the glasshouse using image 1: the narrow slab path leads through naturally overlapping courgette, climbing bean and herb growth; glazing at the right edge, low wall and hedge beyond. Living crops occupy most of frame. Keep small real-garden scale and natural gaps. An inviting observational view rather than a staged display.
2. AT COURGETTE HEIGHT — no person. Closer and lower view of real courgette plants still rooted in the home garden bed, grounded in image 1. Broad matt leaves of different sizes cross each other; one or two modest dark-green courgettes visible where their stems really meet the plant, a yellow flower, darker soil glimpsed below, some adjacent bean/chard foliage. The path/glasshouse only a small contextual hint. Natural plant architecture, no fruit scattered on soil, no giant marrows. Strong sense of being among living plants.
3. THE WORKING ALLOTMENT — no person. Adapt image 3's actual view, at the same low angle along the leeks and slab edge. Differently sized blue-green leaves fan and lean naturally, soil gaps and a netted row behind; a small glimpse of pale green shed/black butt at right. August density, credible stalk thickness, no artificially filled perfect rows. Reduce sky through a portrait crop while preserving the photographed landmarks.
4. AMONG THE CLIMBING BEANS — no person. A closer crop of the living bean row in the actual allotment from image 2, imagined in its productive summer stage. Slender weathered bamboo and naturally irregular heart-shaped leaves; a few modest hanging bean pods, some gaps through to neighbouring planted strips and the pale green shed small in background. Supports rise taller than a person. Use real slender tapering bamboo, modest nodes, small green wire ties, canes rooted in soil not path. No invented elaborate trellis, no perfect cloned rows. The subject is the growing plants, not a support-construction diagram.
5. JOHN QUIETLY TENDING A HOME BED — candid, gardener secondary to the crops. In actual home garden from images 1 and 5, John crouches on the slab path beside a leafy bed, seen obliquely from a little above. He looks down and gently moves one outer leaf to reach the plant beneath; one hand on his knee, the other naturally involved in the job. Pose/profile from real camera panels in image 4, olive T-shirt and shorts from image 5. Foreground leaves partly overlap his lower body naturally, but hands/action remain intelligible. No presenting produce, no smile at camera, no staged portrait. Include enough garden around him to make this a scene, not a close-up of a man.
6. JOHN CHECKING THE BEAN ROW — candid, wider environmental photograph at actual allotment from image 2. John stands side-on in the middle distance, head slightly lowered toward the bean foliage, momentarily checking a hanging pod with one hand while the other lightly steadies the vine. Both feet on the paved/grass access edge, not trampling soil or plants. His accurate natural mature face is small and partly turned away; use image 4 camera profile and image 5 identity/outfit. Canes taller than him, natural bean foliage partly obscures his arm. Several growing plants and a planted strip dominate foreground. Nobody looking at camera, no harvest props, no beaming portrait.

LAYOUT FLEXIBILITY: each photo will eventually carry a large white section title, but NO lettering within these photos now. Where natural, retain a reasonably calm darker upper area of foliage or shade; do not distort the garden into an artificial blank background. Keep main hands/faces/recognisable plant detail away from trim and the bottom 12%, which might later hold a contents strip. The priority is natural SUBJECT AND ACTIVITY, not a stylised arrangement. Six differentiated views in a coherent photographic set. Full image photographic texture, not illustration, and no heavy artificial blur.
